chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away, they heard a voice but did not see a person, saying: 'Every soul shall taste death, but you shall only be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection; then whoever is removed from the Fire and is admitted to Paradise, he indeed has succeeded.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'In Allah is a replacement for every dying one, and a consolation for every bereavement, and a compensation for what is lost. So rely on Allah and hope in Him, and the deprived one is only he who is deprived of the reward.'
ai.seo_question: What is the divine consolation for death and loss according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi contextualizes the Prophet's death not as an end to divine guidance but as a transition to a new era, where Allah serves as the ultimate 'Khalaf' (successor/replacement) for every perishable entity. It highlights the Shia theological emphasis on divine consolation ('Aza') and the certainty of resurrection, framing the Prophet's passing as a test of faith where true loss is defined by missing out on divine reward rather than the physical absence of the leader. The narration reinforces the concept that death is a universal decree, yet spiritual continuity is maintained through Allah's promise of recompense on the Day of Judgment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the Prophetsaww passed away, a voice was heard, and the person was not seen, saying: ‘[3:185] Every self shall taste the death, but rather you shall only be paid fully your Reward on the Day of Judgement; then whoever is removed far away from the Fire and is made to enter the Paradise he indeed has succeeded’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is a replacement from every dying one, and a condolence from every bereavement, and a compensation for what is lost. Thus, on Allah<sup>azwj</sup> you should be relying, and to Him<sup>azwj</sup> should you be hoping, and rather the deprived one is the one deprived of the Rewards’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that when the Messenger of Allah passed away they (people) heard a voice, but did not see anyone in person, saying, ‘Every soul is to experience the taste of death. You will certainly receive your reward on the Day of Judgment. Whoever is saved from the fire and is admitted in paradise, has become successful indeed.’

It also said, ‘In (the mercy of) Allah are good consequences for everyone who dies, solace for all forms of sorrow and compensation for every loss. In Allah, you must trust and in Him only place your hope. Deprived person, in reality, is one who is deprived of the rewards from Allah.’”
